title: Runtime shape compiler and explainable validation for tool parameters
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a runtime 'shape compiler' that converts JSON schema-like tool parameter declarations into a compact executable validation plan, plus an explainable diagnostics layer that maps runtime validation failures to actionable, human-friendly error messages. This ticket focuses on the compilation format, runtime validation API shape, error-code taxonomy, telemetry hooks, and a migration path from existing schema formats.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Compiler accepts current schema DSL (type, required, enum, pattern, properties, items, additionalProperties=false) and produces a compact bytecode-ish plan that reduces repeated parse overhead by >60% on benchmark workloads.

2) Runtime validation API returns structured result with: (a) pass/fail, (b) canonical error_code, (c) human_hint string, (d) pointer path to offending token, (e) suggestion array (optional). All fields must be strings or arrays as specified in spec.

3) Built-in mapping for the 12 most-common user errors (missing required, type mismatch, enum mismatch, pattern failure, extra props blocked, array length bounds, numeric bounds, format/date-time, duplicate keys, unknown enum variant, coercion failure) with deterministic error_code names and recommended remediation hints.

4) End-to-end benchmarks show per-request validation CPU cost reduced by >=50% compared to the present JSON-schema runtime in our internal microbench harness with 100k requests distributed across 8 model-serving threads.
5) Backwards-compatible fallback: if a compiled plan is unavailable for a schema, runtime uses legacy validator; no user-visible change in error semantics during rollout.
6) Telemetry emitted for: compiled_plan_id, validation_latency_ms, error_code (if any), and schema_version. Telemetry keys must match Console/Optimize dashboards conventions.
7) Documentation PR merged describing compiler format, authoring guidelines for schema authors, and migration notes for existing tool manifest authors.
8) Unit and integration tests covering positive/negative cases and fuzz tests for invalid schemas added to CI with >=90% coverage for the compiler module.
discussion: 2025-02-18 | Aisha Patel: Kickoff - goal is to reduce CPU jitter and provide clearer errors for tool-call validation. We observed spikes in token latency due to repeated schema parsing in hot paths.

2025-02-20 | Marco Ruiz: Prototype idea - compile schema into a linear sequence of opcodes (type-check, branch, coerce, emit-error) stored alongside model binding metadata. Will prototype with Go and port to Rust for runtime.
2025-02-24 | Design feedback - PM (Jill Tan) requested that error messages include an end-user remediation hint and a machine-readable error_code that maps to Console breadcrumbs.

2025-02-26 | Trade-off discussion - strict vs permissive validation modes. Decision: default to strict for P0 customers, allow permissive/coercion mode opt-in via route param. Must document semantic differences and telemetry flags.

2025-02-27 | Security note - compiler must not execute arbitrary code from schema. We will restrict schema DSL to declarative constructs only and sandbox parser. Security review flagged potential XSS in suggested hints; sanitize all hints before storing.

2025-02-28 | Infra note - compiled plans will be cached in Redis for hosted; Dedicated/Private deployments will expose local plan cache with eviction policy. Cache key: sha256(schema_text + schema_version).
2025-03-01 | QA feedback - add a translator utility that converts legacy JSON Schema draft-07 constructs we used to author into the new DSL subset. This reduces migration burden.
2025-03-02 | Marco Ruiz: Implemented first pass compiler prototype (Go). Early results: parsing+compile amortized <0.5ms for medium schema; validation runtime reduced 3.5x on microbench.
Follow-ups: add feature flag gating for canary rollout and implement Console UI to show canonical error_code counts per route.
implementation_notes: Compiler format: linear opcodes with small immediate args; encode as varint-prefixed instructions to keep plan compact. Each plan includes a constant pool for enum lists and regex engines compiled ahead-of-time.

Runtime API: Validate(compiledPlanId, jsonPayload) -> {status: 'ok'|'fail', error_code: string|'', pointer: string|'', hint: string|'', suggestions: [string]}. We'll represent pointer as JSON-Pointer string.

Error taxonomy: use namespaced codes like VALIDATION.MISSING_REQUIRED, VALIDATION.TYPE_MISMATCH, VALIDATION.PATTERN_FAILURE, VALIDATION.EXTRA_PROPERTY_BLOCKED, VALIDATION.COERCION_FAILED. Keep list stable across runtime-1.20+.
Coercion strategy: provide deterministic coercion rules (e.g., numeric strings -> number if permissive mode) and emit a WARNING code when coercion occurred. Coercion disabled in strict mode.
Telemetry: emit compact tags: plan_id, schema_checksum, route_id, validation_ms, error_code. Use existing metrics backend naming and include sample-rate knobs to control cardinality.
Caching: store compiled plans with TTL and LRU eviction; fallback to on-the-fly compile when cache miss and mark telemetry as compile_time_ms.
Compatibility: translator tool converts extraneous JSON Schema features into conservative equivalents or rejects with migration hints for authors.
Security hardening: no regexes allowed that can cause ReDoS at large scale; cap regex complexity and execution time. Sanitize all hint strings and escape characters for downstream Console rendering.
qa_plan: Unit tests: validate opcodes against canonical examples, edge cases for arrays, nested objects, and deeply nested pointers.
Fuzz tests: random schema + payload test to assert runtime does not panic and returns a deterministic error_code.
Integration: run validation in-mock under typical request patterns (chat completion + function call) and assert tail latency impact is within SLO.
Regression: run existing test-suite for function-call compatibility to ensure older tool manifests still parse or have clear migration errors.
Security: static analysis on compiler code and regex engine; run load tests to detect ReDoS or parser slowdowns.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Deploy compiler on a small subset of hosted API routes behind feature flag; collect telemetry for errors and compile times. Duration: 1 week.
Phase 2 (gradual): Expand to 20% of routes, enable caching; provide opt-in permissive mode to a subset of customers for migration tests.
Phase 3 (full): Flip default to use compiled plans for all new schemas. Old schemas will be recompiled into plans during a background migration. Provide migration-report in Console.
Rollback: feature flag to fall back to legacy validator, invalidate plan cache keys, and surface migration incidents in on-call channel #infra-compiler.
Communication: Email + Console banner for Dedicated and Private customers explaining changes and how to opt-in/out. Include migration guide link.
